name: correlation-as-inbox-source
text:
`crates/team/src/lib.rs` runs a team. Recording and delivering one message
through `Team::send` rests on two facts about the message: the inbox source it
arrives under, and, when it answers a question, the identity of the question it
answers. A pair of an `InboxSource` and an optional message identifier carries
both facts under the public name `Correlate`, and that pair is the last
argument of `Team::send`. A message that is neither a question nor an answer
arrives as `peer` with no identity. A question arrives as `request` under an
identity of its own. An answer arrives as `response` carrying the identity of
its question, so the asker waits for that answer alone.

The function that reads the arguments of a `send` or an `ask` call builds the
pair: `ask` gives `request` with no identity, `send` with a `reply_to` argument
gives `response` with the identifier that argument names, and `send` without
one gives `peer` with no identity. `Team::send` reads the source and the
identity out of the pair directly. It reuses a named identity as the message
identifier and otherwise allocates one from the lead episode and the recorded
queue length. It appends the text block naming the identifier when the source
is `request`, and it builds the inbox item under that source.

checks/run.sh runs the checks this task is judged on: the tests of foe-team, clippy with warnings denied on the same crates, and scripts/loc.sh.
